Hi Naomi,

Thanks for the draft MSA — please find our redlines attached (Solara_MSA_redline_v1.pdf). A few high-level points from legal:

- We need Redwood to defend and indemnify Solara for third-party IP claims arising from the delivery or use of the Services, including patent and copyright claims.
- We expect defense control for Solara where the claim relates to our specific use case, or at minimum a right to participate with counsel of our choosing.
- We have an insurance / financial cap expectation: either a $5M supplier liability or limits tied to annual fees.
- We need explicit carveouts for open-source components and for any customer data we supply.

Can your team propose workable language and confirm whether Redwood will accept defense control or provide a limited carveout? We have a signing target the week of Dec 6.

Attachment: Solara_MSA_redline_v1.pdf (pdf)

Regards,

Hi Lydia — thanks for the redlines and the clear summary. Appreciate the signing target. Quick response while our legal team reviews:

Option A (preferred, lower commercial impact): Redwood will defend and indemnify against third-party IP claims that specifically allege that the hosted Service as delivered by Redwood infringes a third party's patents or copyrights, subject to the exceptions for OSS and customer-provided content. Redwood requests the right to control the defense (choice of counsel, settlement authority) but will not settle any claim that imposes injunctive relief on Solara without prior consent.

Option B (alternatively): Redwood accepts a mutual defense with carveouts: Solara may control defense if the claim relates to customizations Solara made to prompts or post-processing.

We can also propose a $5M indemnity bucket or tie to the order-form fees if you prefer. I've attached our initial response redline for your review.

Attachment: Redwood_MSA_response_v1.pdf (pdf)

Ben — can you confirm if a limited commercial credit to cover an indemnity cap increase is feasible?

Best,

Naomi / Ben — looping in Rishi and adding legal position for negotiation. Key points:

1) Defense control: Redwood prefers control of defense for operational reasons (we run the infra, have the logs, and can coordinate technical response). We can allow Solara to participate with separate counsel at their cost and to veto settlements that materially affect Solara's business, but allowing Solara unilateral control increases risk and cost.

2) Scope of indemnity: We will offer indemnity for third-party claims that directly allege infringement by Redwood's Service as provided (i.e., not claims based solely on how Solara used the Service or on customer data you supplied). We need express carveouts for: (a) OSS licensed components; (b) third-party models or weights you bring; (c) prompts or tooling you build on top.

3) Monetary cap & insurance: propose provider cap = greater of $5M or 12 months of fees, with a commitment to maintain $5M commercial general liability / tech E&O as applicable. This is consistent with comparable customers.

4) Notice & cooperation: 10 business days' notice after becoming aware; Redwood to lead and share evidence. We'll need your help preserving logs and providing relevant inputs.

5) Settlement authority: Redwood will not settle on behalf of Solara without Solara's consent if the settlement imposes operational constraints or a continuing obligation. Redwood can settle purely monetary amounts to limit exposure if Solara does not want to participate.

Attachment: (internal) evidence_list_and_playbook.txt — internal checklist (not for Solara).

If you want, we can propose concrete redline text that captures the above and mark it as compromise language for the MSA. Naomi, if Solara insists on defense control, we'll need a commercial concession (higher cap or credit).

-Marissa

Subject: Final compromise language proposal & next steps (Solara Health / SOL-4721)

Lydia — thanks for the quick turn. Based on the thread below we propose the following compromise to close in time for your Dec 6 target: 

- Scope: Redwood will indemnify and defend Solara from third-party claims alleging that the Redwood-hosted Service as delivered infringes a third party's patents or copyrights, excluding claims based on (i) open-source components (as listed in Appendix A), (ii) customer-provided models or weights, or (iii) customer-modified prompts/control logic.

- Defense control & participation: Redwood will control the defense and selection of counsel, provided that Solara may (a) participate with separate counsel at its own expense, and (b) withhold consent to any settlement that (i) imposes an injunction or continuing operational restriction on Solara, or (ii) requires the assignment of Solara's intellectual property. Redwood will not unreasonably withhold consent to monetary settlements intended to resolve the claim.

- Cap & insurance: Provider indemnity cap = the greater of $5,000,000 or 12 months of fees paid under the applicable order form. Redwood will maintain $5,000,000 in applicable liability coverage and provide certificate upon execution. Statutory damages for willful copyright infringement will be subject to the cap but will be escalated to exec review prior to settlement.

- Notice & cooperation: Solara will notify Redwood within 10 business days of receipt of claim notice. Both parties will preserve logs and cooperate; Redwood will share the evidence preservation checklist.

Attached is a redline reflecting this language: Redwood_MSA_final_redline_20271130.pdf (pdf). If this captures your concerns, Ben will confirm the commercial concession (order-form credit / fee adjustment) and we can route the final order form via DocuSign. HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.example.com/deals/SOL-4721.

- Ben: confirm commercial trade (credit vs higher cap) and let procurement know we need a signed order form.
